title: Role-variable releases: /ops opens the design-system lock for a release whose v8 preview reading is clean, and keeps it shut while VARS-1 or MODE-3 fails
steps: S1: Derive the customer lock from the stored /ops Design system checks (readyTemplates) for a release whose rules all pass, and for one where a must-fix rule fails, a rule is unmeasured, the check is running or never ran.
S2: Grade a release with checkRelease when its role scan is missing, clean, or names missing roles and hardcoded literals (VARS-1).
S3: Grade a release whose measurement, contract or stylesheets show a light/dark switch while its contract offers one look, and a two-mode contract (MODE-3).
S4: Grade a release whose preview was re-measured in the tree (probe v8) after its VERIFICATION.json was written.
expect: S1: only an all-pass check opens the template (code ds-ready); every other state keeps it shut with its own code.
S2: VARS-1 is must-fix for every CMS; no scan for this version is Not scanned yet and holds Publish; missing roles and literals fail naming file, line and component; a clean scan passes.
S3: MODE-3 is must-fix for every CMS and fails on each one-look mismatch; modes: true passes; a one-look template is not applicable.
S4: the newest in-tree preview reading wins over the release VERIFICATION.json of the same run.
evidence: Unit tests over the /ops lock derivation and the VARS-1, MODE-3 and measurement readers that the role-variable batch added or changed
fence: Lock derivation and rule grading in tracy-web; does not drive a stand or a browser
